links.comparator_used: Untuned cost-sensitive bagged trees (CSBT-Untuned) at its default threshold
links.outcome: Minority-class (opioid misuse) detection and Clinical Discriminative Performance Score under sensitivity-priority scenarios
links.effect: CSBT-Untuned had the highest raw accuracy (86.7%) but missed 61.5% of positive cases. Threshold-optimized CSBT-Tuned had enhanced minority class detection and numerically higher Clinical Discriminative Performance Scores, statistically comparable to RUSBoost given overlapping confidence intervals.
links.tradeoff: CSBT-Untuned had the highest raw accuracy, so threshold tuning gave up some raw accuracy. The CDPS advantage was only numerical, not statistically significant against RUSBoost.
links.quote: Conversely, the threshold-optimized CSBT-Tuned model achieved enhanced minority class detection and numerically higher Clinical Discriminative Performance Scores under sensitivity-priority scenarios, though its performance remained statistically comparable to RUSBoost given overlapping confidence intervals.

design_hint: alert threshold selection with cost-sensitive clinical evaluation
